# Data Understanding {#sec-02-data-understanding}

## Identification of Data Sources

<!-- Describe what data is available and where it comes from. -->

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-sources
#| echo: false
#| include: true


library(data.table)
library(kableExtra)

# Read the data into a data.table 
dtDS <-  fread(text = "
  Data Source         , Time-Span, Granularity, Speciality
  article master data , > 2020 ,            , article hierachy
  customer master data, > 2020 ,            , customer hierachy
  historical sales    , > 2020 , daily      , customer orders + free-of-charge 
  historical forecasts, > 2023 , monhtly    , monthly forecasts for each month in 2024, before- and after demand review
")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtDS |> 
  kbl(
    caption   = "Data Sources ",
    col.names = names(dtDS),
    align     = c("l", "l", "l"),
    booktabs  = TRUE
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position   = "left",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )
```

## Initial Data Collection Report

<!-- Summarize how data was obtained and any issues during acquisition: -->

All data is Sourced from *BioBalance* SAP-BI system using the SAP Open Hub Technology.

![Data Collection pipelines](/images/dp01.png){#dp01 fig-align="center"}

The data is extracted from the underlying tables, joined, filtered and transformed and written to a CSV file.

<!-- Data filters applied (Doctype's, Item category, ...) -->

<!-- exclude units pak and DS   -->

BUOM <!-- exclude Promotion articles --> PRAT7 <!-- only master data which is relevant for the analysis -->

<!-- DuckDB tranformations -->

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-collection
#| echo: false
#| include: true


library(data.table)
library(kableExtra)

# Read the data into a data.table 
dtDC <-  fread(text = "
  Data Source         , Type, Extract Date, Records, GB  , Key
  article master data , MD  ,             ,        ,     , Article     
  customer master data, MD  ,             ,        ,     , Customer
  historical sales    , TD  ,             ,        ,     , Date; Article; Plant; Customer
  historical forecasts, TD  ,             ,        ,     , Date; Article; Plant; CustHier3
")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtDC |> 
  kbl(
    caption   = "Data Collection ",
    col.names = names(dtDC),
    align     = c("l", "l", "l"),
    booktabs  = TRUE
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position   = "left",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )
```

<!-- Hierarchies (e.g., 4-level product and customer trees) -->

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-description-hierarchy
#| echo: false
#| include: true

library(ggplot2)
library(openxlsx2)
library(data.table)
library(magrittr)

OD <- "C:\\Users\\flori\\OneDrive\\ET\\pythia\\data"

# Read the data into a data.table
dtMAT <- wb_read(
  file      = file.path(OD, "ET2BB.xlsx"),
  sheet     = "MASP",
  start_row = 19,
  start_col = 6,
  skip_empty_cols = TRUE,
  skip_empty_rows = TRUE
) %T>%
  setDT() %T>%
  setnames(c(2,4,6,8), c("level1", "level2", "level3", "level4")) 

dt <- copy(dtMAT)

```

::: {# .figure}
::: {.content-visible when-format="html"} 
```{r}
library(collapsibleTree)

collapsibleTree(
  dt,
  hierarchy = c("level2", "level3", "level4"),
  root      = "Products",
  width     = "100%",
  zoomable  = TRUE
)
```
 
::: 
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
```{r}
library(treemapify)

# Count of level4 items per level1/level2 combo
treemap_dt <- dt[, .N, by = .(level1, level2, level3, level4)]
treemap_dt[, count := .N, by = .(level1, level2)]

# Use only level1-level2 for compactness
ggplot(treemap_dt, aes(area = count, fill = level1, label = level2)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_text(colour = "white", place = "centre", grow = TRUE) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


```
